T lymphocytes from scleroderma patients produce higher levels of reactive oxygen species than healthy controls, which are mainly generated by the NADPH oxidases complex via the activation of the MAP kinase ERK1/ 2, and are essential for cell proliferation, activation, and cytokine secretion.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SSc T lymphocyte activation, proliferation, cytokine production, and ROS generation are interdependent processes, all of which contribute to the pathogenesis of the disease.
the study of oxidative stress in T lymphocytes is a key point in the pathogenesis and progression of systemic sclerosis.

the increased oxidative stress in Ssc is due to the activation of NADPH-oxidase, which is a complex enzyme composed of 5 subunits, 2 of which are membrane bound (gp91phox and p22phox) and 3 are cytosolic (p40phox, p47phox and p67phox).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oxidative stress in the SSc T lymphocyte is a consequence of the increased NADPH oxidases activity, and this increased activity is a consequence of ERK1/ and 2 phosphorylation.
the increased ROS production in SSc T lymphoctyes is due to an increased NADPH oxidases activity, that leads to an increased T cells proliferation and activation.
SSc T cells are characterized by high ROS production and that this is mediated by NADPH complex via ERK1-2 phosphorylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ROS are produced in SSc peripheral blood T cells by NADPH Oxidase and ERK 1/2 phosphorylating pathway.
T cells from SSc patients are characterized by an abnormal oxidative stress that may contribute to the development of the disease.
ROS are produced by SSc T lymphocyte via NADPH oxidases and ERK1.2 activation and this is essential for cell activation and cytokine production.
